description: Foundation entries for the capability-first Blacklight Continuum d10 system. The rules measure what a character can do, not what they are made of or how they arrived.

entries.title: Blacklight Original d10 System Foundation
entries.summary: An original Attribute-plus-Skill d10 framework supporting operatives, supernatural Archetypes, advanced technology, Exposure, equipment, investigation, social conflict, and dangerous field operations.
body: Build a test pool from Attribute + Skill + situational modifiers. Results of 6 through 9 produce one success. A 10 produces one success and may activate a specialization, equipment quality, or power rider. A failed roll containing one or more 1s creates a Complication.

Difficulty normally ranges from one to five successes. Characters may Push by rerolling failed dice up to Resolve, then gain Exposure representing accumulated risk, cognitive strain, supernatural attention, operational instability, or psychological pressure according to the scene.

The core rules never grant or deny abilities because of descriptive anatomy, species, substrate, printing material, appearance, or arrival history. A capability exists only when an Attribute, Skill, Archetype feature, power, equipment item, condition, or explicit narrative permission says it exists.

The current rules remain an alpha foundation. Combat, advancement, power trees, equipment, and character-sheet interfaces are active development areas, but capability-first design is a permanent system principle.

entries.title: Capability Framework
entries.summary: All exceptional effects are defined by capabilities, costs, limits, resistance, and outcomes.
body: A capability is anything a character can reliably attempt beyond ordinary untrained action: a supernatural power, professional technique, technological interface, ritual, transformation, resistance, special sense, movement mode, social authority, or other explicit permission.
The rules ask what the capability does, what pool activates it, what it costs, how long it lasts, what resists it, and what happens on failure.

Two characters may describe the same mechanical capability through different sources. Two characters with similar appearances or origins gain no shared mechanical benefit unless both possess the relevant capability.

Archetypes organize exceptional capability families. Operational Frames organize professional competence. Equipment supplies external functions. Conditions temporarily add, restrict, or alter capabilities.

Ability descriptions use fixed outcomes or closed choice menus. The Game Moderator applies established targets, hazards, and world facts, but an activated ability does not require the moderator to invent its benefit, scope, duration, or ordinary failure consequence.

entries.title: Character Creation Foundation
entries.summary: Characters are built from present identity, Attributes, Skills, Operational Frame, Archetype, powers, limitations, relationships, equipment, and explicit capabilities.
body: Define the character's present concept, current occupation or function, affiliation, defining conviction, important relationship, professional obligation, personal boundary, and one debt, promise, or contract.
Assign one Attribute at 4, three at 3, three at 2, and two at 1. Assign three Skills at 3, five at 2, five at 1, and the rest at 0. Choose three specializations.

Choose an Operational Frame, an Archetype, a Lineage or Variant when appropriate, starting powers according to the campaign's allocation rules, one signature capability, and one meaningful limitation or bane.
Record every rules-relevant benefit as an Attribute, Skill, specialization, innate ability, power, Operational Frame feature, equipment feature, condition, or explicit narrative permission.
The printer produced the selected human or human-adjacent character from the supplied construction definition. Character creation begins with that character’s present capabilities.

entries.title: Equipment and Salvage Foundation
entries.summary: Equipment is defined by quality, function, tags, limits, access, and interface requirements.
body: Equipment quality ranges from Improvised through Serviceable, Professional, Advanced, and Exceptional. Better quality improves reliability, adds dice in a defined role, or changes what actions are possible.
The team initially obtains equipment from maintenance tools, emergency stores, damaged compartments, recovered technology, fabrication systems, remote manipulators, and printed replacements.

Items must state a clear operating effect, quality, tags, limitations, interface requirements, and resource dependence. A character can use an item when they possess the required capability, training, access, or adapter.
When equipment requires a particular interface, scale, environment, authority, or support system, record that restriction explicitly as a tag.
